system.name: EnergyWatch AI
system.description: Multi-agent assistant that monitors the energy consumption of four sites (office, factory, data center, clinic), detects anomalies, recommends grounded energy-saving actions and keeps a human in the loop for any operational change.
intended_use: Answer energy managers' questions about consumption, cost, CO2 and peaks
Detect and explain abnormal consumption (leaks, schedules, drifts, faults)
Recommend energy-efficiency actions grounded in a curated knowledge base
Queue proposed actions for human approval with a full audit trail
out_of_scope: Direct control of equipment (the system is read-only on the infrastructure)
Safety-critical decisions in clinical areas without the facility manager
Financial or contractual advice on electricity contracts
Questions unrelated to energy (blocked by the guardrails)
system.architecture: LangGraph supervisor pattern: guardrails -> supervisor (planner) -> specialists -> report_writer -> monitor

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Pattern-based input guardrail before any LLM call; security incident RB-003 on bursts
Output scanning for credentials, PII redaction in logs, no secrets in prompts
Read-only tools; medium/high-risk actions require human approval; audit trail
Numbers come from deterministic tools; prompts forbid invented facts; recommendations cite sources
Input length limit, per-client rate limiting, timeouts, circuit breaker
Retries + circuit breaker + deterministic degraded mode (runbook RB-001)

system.observability: Correlation ID on every request/run/log/span/incident/audit entry; Prometheus metrics at /metrics; run explorer in the dashboard
system.contact: Open an issue on the GitHub repository

agents.name: Guardrails Agent
agents.description: Validates every question before it reaches an LLM: prompt-injection patterns, length limit, control characters, and topic scope (energy only).
agents.autonomy: Fully automatic; blocks but never acts
agents.human_oversight: Blocked queries are visible in the run explorer (status=blocked) and in the audit log
agents.limitations: Regex-based; does not detect semantically disguised injections

agents.name: Supervisor / Planner Agent
agents.description: Classifies the intent (consumption, anomaly, advice, report), detects the site and time window, and plans which specialist agents run, using structured output validated by a Pydantic schema.
agents.human_oversight: Plan and reasoning are shown in the dashboard trace for every run
agents.fallback: Deterministic keyword planner (also used in mock mode); output is sanitized (allowed agents only, valid site IDs, 1-30 days)

agents.name: Consumption Analyst Agent
agents.description: Chooses and calls read-only data tools (tool calling) to compute consumption, cost, CO2, peak demand, period comparisons, top consumers and data-center PUE, then summarizes the results.
agents.human_oversight: Tool calls are listed in the run trace
agents.fallback: Rule-based tool selection and template narrative; tool errors trigger runbook RB-004

agents.name: Anomaly Detector Agent
agents.description: Runs statistical detection (robust z-score against a per-hour, per-day-type baseline learned on 14 days), classifies the pattern (night/weekend operation, sustained increase, drift, spike), quantifies excess kWh and cost, and explains likely root causes.
agents.human_oversight: Anomalies are listed in the dashboard with severity and cost
failure_modes: False positives after a legitimate schedule change
agents.fallback: Template explanation with a root-cause table
metrics: precision / recall on injected anomalies (evaluation suite)
agents.limitations: Baseline must be re-learned after structural changes on a site

agents.name: Energy Advisor Agent (RAG)
agents.description: Retrieves relevant sections of the energy-efficiency knowledge base (BM25 with query expansion), writes recommendations with citations and estimated savings, and proposes actions to the human-in-the-loop queue.
agents.permissions: read-only data; may PROPOSE actions, never execute them
agents.autonomy: Low-risk actions are auto-approved by policy; medium/high-risk actions wait for an operator
agents.human_oversight: Approve / reject in the dashboard (Actions page); every decision is audited
agents.limitations: Knowledge base is a curated set of 7 documents; savings are estimates

agents.name: Report Writer Agent
agents.description: Combines the specialists' outputs into one Markdown answer with a headline, keeps every number and citation, flags degraded mode, and passes the output through the output guardrail.
agents.human_oversight: Answer shown with its full trace and correlation ID
agents.fallback: Template report assembled from the specialists' sections

agents.name: Monitoring Agent
agents.description: Wraps every agent to record spans linked to the correlation ID, evaluates each run against the SLOs, updates metrics, and opens / resolves incidents following the runbook (RB-001 LLM outage, RB-002 latency, RB-003 injection burst, RB-004 tool failure).
agents.permissions: write access to telemetry stores only
agents.autonomy: Automatic detection and mitigation; incident closure is automatic or by an operator
agents.human_oversight: Monitoring page of the dashboard; incidents can be resolved manually
failure_modes: Telemetry stored in memory is lost on restart
agents.fallback: Structured JSON logs on stdout are the durable source of truth (collected by the platform)
agents.limitations: In-memory stores (single instance); use an external TSDB / tracing backend to scale out
